newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-IRELAND'S FRANK STAPLETON QUITS AS MLS COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRELAND'S FRANK STAPLETON QUITS AS MLS COACH.

text.p: Irish soccer legend Frank Stapleton resigned as coach of the New England Revolution on Thursday, five days after the team failed to qualify for the Major League Soccer playoffs.
"I had been mulling it over for the last 24 hours," said Stapleton, "and after taking everything into consideration and discussing it with my family, I decided to resign."

Stapleton, the all-time leading scorer for Ireland with 20 goals in 71 internationals, had previously been assistant coach for Queens Park Rangers in the English Premier League (1994-95) and was player-coach for Huddersfield Town and Bradford City.
Stapleton, 40, was named coach of the Revolution in January. The team finished last in the Eastern Conference and ninth overall in the 10-team league with a 15-17 record.

"The management tried to persuade me to stay," Stapleton said, "but having thought about it, knowing that I didn't want to put my family through a difficult time, and for my future career, I decided to step down."
Stapleton was not a favourite of the fans or the Boston-area media this season and was criticised for his team's lack of success and inconsistent play on the field.

"This has been a tough situation all the way around," said New England General Manager Brian O'Donovan. "Frank found it tough to come back and collectively we talked about it and ultimately he came to the decision that it would be better for him to resign due to the situation."
"I feel sorry for him and his family that it didn't work out here," said New England and U.S. international defender Alexi Lalas, who was at odds with Stapleton all season.

"Given the circumstances and our history together, anything I say would be considered trite, but I wish him success. From a player's point of view, it is important that we realise that we bear an equal amount of the blame for the season."
Stapleton is the fifth coach to resign or be fired in the league's inaugural season.

Timo Liekoski (Columbus), Eddie Firmani (New York/New Jersey) and Bobby Houghton (Colorado) are already out of the league and Carlos Quieroz (NY/NJ) is in the playoffs but has opted to coach in Japan next year.
Stapleton captained Ireland for 30 matches and helped lead the team to qualification for the 1988 European Championships and 1990 World Cup.

He began his career as an apprentice for Arsenal in 1973 and made his first-team debut in 1975. In 1981 he joined Manchester United and played for seven years at Old Trafford before joining Dutch powerhouse Ajax. Stapleton also played with LeHavre in France before he was transferred to Blackburn Rovers in 1989. He finished his career with Bradford City.
